name: Aberdeen North Foodbank
description: Part of The Trussell Trust network providing emergency food parcels to residents in crisis. Works with local agencies for referrals.
address: Unit 15 Apex Living Centre Springtown Industrial Est Londonderry

name: Seaton Park Wild Garlic
short_description: Wild garlic in the riverside woodland at Seaton Park.
description: Dense carpets of wild garlic grow along the wooded banks of the River Don within Seaton Park each spring. Best picked before flowering in April.

name: Hazlehead Park Community Orchard
short_description: Public orchard in the grounds of Hazlehead Park.
description: Apple, plum and damson trees are accessible to the public in the orchard area near the maze. Surplus fruit is free to take.

name: Incredible Edible Aberdeen (Rosemount)
short_description: Community edible planters on Rosemount Place.
description: Street-side planters maintained by local volunteers growing kale, chard, herbs and edible flowers for anyone to pick freely.

name: River Dee Path Blackberries
short_description: Brambles along the lower River Dee walkway.
description: Extensive blackberry brambles line the public footpath along the south bank of the River Dee between Ruthrieston and Cults.

name: Scotstown Moor Wild Bilberries
short_description: Bilberries on the open heathland of Scotstown Moor.
description: Wild bilberries (blaeberries) ripen on the heathland paths of Scotstown Moor Local Nature Reserve in late summer.

name: Tillydrone Community Growing Project
short_description: Shared community veg beds open to all.
description: A community-run growing project with raised vegetable beds. Surplus produce including courgettes, beans and salad is left out for free during harvest season.

name: Donmouth Local Nature Reserve Elderberries
short_description: Elder trees at the River Don estuary mouth.
description: Elder trees grow along the dune and scrub margins of Donmouth LNR. Elderflower in June and ripe berries from late August.

name: Nigg Bay Coastal Sea Beet
short_description: Sea beet on the rocky shoreline at Nigg Bay.
description: Wild sea beet grows on the rocky coastal margins south of the harbour. Tender young leaves can be picked from spring through to autumn.

name: Victoria Park Allotment Surplus Stall
short_description: Honesty-box surplus veg from Victoria Park allotments.
description: Local plot holders put surplus vegetables and soft fruit on an honesty-box table at the allotment gate throughout the growing season.

name: Brimmond Hill Blaeberries
short_description: Wild blaeberries on the Brimmond Hill moorland.
description: Open heathland on Brimmond Hill is rich with wild blaeberry (bilberry) bushes. A popular foraging walk with good views over the city.

name: Torry Community Growing Space
short_description: Raised beds in Torry with free surplus produce.
description: Community raised beds growing seasonal vegetables in the heart of Torry. Excess produce is left on a free-sharing table at weekends.

name: Loirston Country Park Sloes
short_description: Blackthorn hedgerows at Loirston Country Park.
description: Blackthorn scrub around the edges of Loirston Loch produces a reliable crop of sloes each autumn, best after the first hard frost.

name: Westburn Park Community Orchard
short_description: Public fruit trees in Westburn Park.
description: Crab apple and cherry trees throughout Westburn Park are freely accessible. The crab apples make excellent jelly and are ripe from September.

name: Persley Den Wild Garlic and Hazelnuts
short_description: Mixed foraging in the wooded gorge of Persley Den.
description: The wooded banks of the River Don at Persley Den support wild garlic carpets in spring and hazel trees bearing nuts by September.
